claims.head: The Hurricanes will send Slavin and Chatfield at Pastrňák
claims.call: The Hurricanes’ P2 (Slavin and Chatfield) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Bruins’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Hurricanes keep sending Slavin and Chatfield out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rod Brind'Amour has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Bruins’ first line is Peterka, Zacha and Pastrňák.

claims.head: Forecheck against patience
claims.body: The Hurricanes hound the puck, but the Bruins sit back. Carolina is one of the league’s best for forecheck pressure, and Boston is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Hurricanes to win more pucks back deep in the Bruins’ end.

notes.text: Michael Eyssimont has not played this season. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Connor Clifton has not dressed for the last 5 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Will Borgen has taken his spot beside Nikita Zadorov.
Mark Jankowski is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Taylor Hall is on injured reserve and has missed the last 4 games. Nikolaj Ehlers has taken his spot beside Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake.
Seth Jarvis returned in their last game after missing 5 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Bradly Nadeau was added to the roster on Oct 15 and has played beside Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake.
Felix Unger Sörum was added to the roster on Oct 17 and has played beside Jordan Martinook and Nikolaj Ehlers.
Skyler Brind'Amour was added to the roster on Oct 23 and has played beside Nicolas Deslauriers and Eric Robinson.
Seth Jarvis was added to the roster on Oct 23 and has played beside Jordan Martinook and Jesperi Kotkaniemi.
Logan Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 33% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, up from 1% last season.

CAR.head: This one sets up well for the Hurricanes
CAR.body: Even though Carolina may be without Jankowski, the Hurricanes have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Bruins’ best way in is getting good looks.

BOS.head: A steep climb for the Bruins
BOS.body: Even though Carolina may be without Jankowski, the Hurricanes have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Bruins’ best hope is getting good looks, plus a big night in goal.

story.head: Two of the best
paras: The Bruins come in at 8-2-1, the Hurricanes at 8-2-2. Two of the league’s best teams meet.
At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Bruins’ first line. The Bruins make their shots count, and the Hurricanes allow dangerous ones.
